# Comic Builder

> A generic, static comic-builder web app. It renders a comic project — pages,
> panels, image layers, and speech bubbles — from a JSON project file. It is not
> tied to any one comic: point it at any project file and it renders that.
>
> Images and the project file live on the user's own Google Drive; the app is a
> static site and talks to Drive client-side via Google OAuth (drive.file scope:
> only files the app created or the user opened with it).
>
> Drive is the only project source. The app opens behind a Drive connect gate —
> the editor is unreachable until the user connects — and every change
> autosaves to `project.json` in the project folder (~2 seconds after the last
> edit). There are no manual open/save buttons in the UI.

## Driving the app as an agent

The app exposes a command API on `window.comicBuilder` once it has loaded. This
is the primary way for an AI agent — or any script running in the page — to
operate the app instead of clicking through the UI. Start with
`comicBuilder.help()`.

Commands (synchronous unless noted):

- `comicBuilder.version` — API version string
- `comicBuilder.help()` — one-line description of every command
- `comicBuilder.getProject()` — current ComicProject as an object (null while loading)
- `comicBuilder.exportProject()` — current project as a JSON string (null while loading)
- `comicBuilder.loadProject(json)` — replace the whole project with validated JSON
  (object or JSON string); returns `{ ok, error? }`
- `comicBuilder.getPageCount()` / `comicBuilder.getPageIndex()` / `comicBuilder.selectPage(i)`
  — page navigation; `selectPage` takes a 0-based index and returns false when out of range
- `comicBuilder.getCurrentPage()` — the shown page as an object (null while loading)
- `comicBuilder.saveLocal()` — persist to the browser's localStorage; returns an ISO
  timestamp, or null when there is nothing to save
- `comicBuilder.saveToDrive()` — async; flush any pending autosave to Drive
  immediately; returns `{ ok, error? }`
- `comicBuilder.openFromDrive()` — async; reload `project.json` from the Drive
  folder, discarding unsaved changes; returns `{ ok, error? }`
- `comicBuilder.getStatus()` — last human-readable status line shown in the UI
- `comicBuilder.driveStatus()` — `{ connected, configured }`

Example session (paste into the browser console, or run via automation):

```js
const p = comicBuilder.getProject();          // read
p.pages[1].title = "The Hallway";             // edit the data, not the DOM
const r = comicBuilder.loadProject(p);        // validate + render; r.ok === true
// no save call needed — the app autosaves to Drive ~2s after the change
```

## Data model

- `ComicProject`: `{ id, title, pages[], updatedAt }`
- `ComicPage`: `{ id, number, title, panels[] }` — `number` is 0-based; the UI shows
  it as `00`, `01`, `02`, …
- `Panel`: `{ id, title?, layers[], bubbles[] }`
- `Layer`: `{ id, name, kind: "background" | "foreground", src, driveFileId?,
  visible, x, y, width, rotation, opacity }` — `x`/`y`/`width` are percentages of
  the panel; aspect ratio is always preserved, never stretched
- `Bubble`: `{ id, kind: "speech" | "thought" | "caption", text, x, y, width,
  tailX?, tailY? }`

Machine-readable schema: `schema/comic-project.schema.json` (JSON Schema, draft 2020-12).
Minimal example project: `data/sample-project.json`.

## Capabilities and limits — read before acting

- Drive-gated and autosaving: the editor only appears after the user connects
  Google Drive, and every project change (UI or `loadProject()`) is written to
  `project.json` in the project folder ~2 seconds after the last edit. There are
  no open/save buttons in the UI. `saveToDrive()` only flushes a pending
  autosave early; `openFromDrive()` reloads from Drive, discarding unsaved changes.

- Rendering is currently read-only in the UI: layers and bubbles are displayed, not
  drag-edited. To change artwork, layout, or text, build a new project JSON and load
  it with `loadProject()` — geometry (`x`/`y`/`width`/`rotation`/`opacity`,
  visibility, stacking order) is preserved exactly as given.
- `loadProject()` replaces the whole project. There is no partial or page-level
  patch API yet: read the project, modify the object client-side, and load the full
  result. When the user talks about one specific page, change only that page's data
  and keep everything else byte-identical.
- Google Drive: the first "Connect Drive" click must come from a real user gesture —
  browsers block programmatic OAuth popups, so an agent cannot complete the connect
  step alone. Ask the user to click "Connect Google Drive". Once connected,
  `saveToDrive()` / `openFromDrive()` work without further clicks.
- Drive access tokens last ~1 hour and are held only in memory — never in
  web storage. Reloading the page drops the token, so the user clicks
  "Connect Google Drive" once per browser session; when a token expires the
  user is asked to reconnect.
- Local saves go to `localStorage` under `cb_local_project`; the previous copy is
  always kept as `cb_local_project_backup`. Never silently discard the backup.
- Never invent layer image URLs. Use `src` values already in the project, `data:` URLs
  you generated, or `driveFileId`s of files that exist in the project folder.

## Key URLs (relative to the site root)

- `/` — the app
- `/llms.txt` — this file
- `/schema/comic-project.schema.json` — JSON Schema of the project model
- `/data/sample-project.json` — minimal example project
